newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity's new president appoints executives.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity's new president appoints executives.

text.p: The new president of Fidelity Investments' mutual fund division moved quickly Wednesday to stem an exodus of portfolio managers by appointing three senior executives to oversee day-to-say support operations.
Robert Pozen, promoted last week to head Fidelity's 251 mutual funds, named three executives, including Abigail Johnson, daughter of Fidelity Chairman Ned Johnson, to focus on operational areas.

The three will "not only review funds but take off the back of the portfolio managers all the non-stock-picking functions and allow the mangers to concentrate on stock-picking," Pozen told Reuters in an interview.

William Hayes, chief operating officer of equity investments, and his assistant Bart Grenier had performed many of those functions on an informal basis. Fidelity confirmed Wednesday that Hayes, 62, would retire by the end of the year. Grenier resigned earlier this month to join another firm.
In addition to Johnson, Fidelity named Robert Lawrence, head of Fidelity's high-income division, and Richard Spillane, former chief investment officer for Europe, to the new management team.
"These are three people who are well known to the portfolio managers and I feel like they've already reacted very favourably to it," Pozen said.

The appointments may limit any opposition among the portfolio managers to the appointment of Pozen, who was formerly Fidelity's legal counsel and had no investment management experience, analysts said.
Johnson, Lawrence and Spillane will focus on operational areas, including systems, trading, recruitment, research and human resources, as well as general fund oversight, Fidelity said.
"I think Bob is putting in place a management group to stabilise the ship," said Eric Kobren, publisher of the independent newsletter Fidelity Insight.

"I think having a little bit more hierarchy, though I know it's a bad word to a lot of people, I think these people will add value in supporting the fund managers, giving them the tools they need," he said.

Analysts said the additional help will bolster the ranks of fund managers, who have been shaken by the departure of 24 portfolio heads in the last 18 months or so. Many of Fidelity's best-known funds have also been underperforming their peers over the last year.
"Obviously, what everyone is waiting for is, 'Are the defections going to slow down?'" said Russel Kinnel, equity fund editor at Morningstar Mutual Funds.
The appointment of Johnson, Fidelity's largest shareholder, moves her closer to the chief executive's seat, but analysts still wonder if she will ascend to CEO.

"I honestly do not believe that Abby knows what she wants to do and whether she wants to take over the company," newsletter publisher Kobren said. "I think she's testing the waters and she's seeing what's going on."
Johnson will continue as group leader of the specialised growth group. Fidelity announced Spillane will become group leader of the Income Growth group whle overseeing the international group.
